title: GPT-4o: One Model for Text, Audio, and Vision
hook: GPT-4o is a single model that natively processes text, audio, and images end-to-end - no separate speech pipeline - cutting voice response latency to near human conversational speed.
key_points: One unified model handles text, audio, and image input and output natively, without chaining separate models.
Voice latency dropped to roughly 232 ms average, close to natural human response time.
Removes the old pipeline of speech-to-text → LLM → text-to-speech, so tone and emotion are preserved end-to-end.
GPT-4-level text and vision performance while being faster and cheaper than GPT-4 Turbo.
content_html: OpenAI announced GPT-4o (the "o" stands for omni) in May 2024 as a single model trained end-to-end across text, audio, and vision. Previous voice features in ChatGPT stitched together three separate models; GPT-4o handles all modalities in one pass. The result is noticeably lower latency and better responsiveness to vocal cues like tone and pace.
extra_html:
How it works

Rather than routing audio through a speech recognizer into a language model and back out through a speech synthesizer, GPT-4o processes audio tokens directly alongside text and image tokens. This unified training means the model sees emotional and prosodic information that gets discarded in a transcription pipeline.

Why it matters

Native omni-modality is a meaningful architectural step: it lets a single model reason jointly across senses without information loss at pipeline boundaries. For voice applications, near-human response latency changes the feel of an interaction entirely. See OpenAI's announcement for demos and details.

related.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
related.hook: GPT-4 clears the bar on a wide range of professional and academic benchmarks - passing the bar exam near the top of the score range, for instance - while accepting both text and images as input.

related.title: CLIP: Learning Visual Models from Language
related.hook: Skip the fixed label list. Train on image–caption pairs so pictures and text share one space, and you can classify images from plain-text labels you make up on the spot.

related.title: Whisper: Robust Speech Recognition at Scale
related.hook: Train a plain encoder-decoder transformer on 680,000 hours of weakly-labeled multilingual audio and you get near-human transcription robustness without task-specific fine-tuning.
